html:
The Kaxixó are a small Indigenous people of Minas Gerais in southeastern Brazil, living around the towns of Martinho Campos and Pompéu, west of Belo Horizonte. In the 2010s they numbered about 300.

Little is known of their history before the colonial period. The interior of Minas Gerais was flooded with settlers during the gold rush of the 1700s, and its native peoples lost most of their land and languages. The Kaxixó survived as farm workers on the estates that took their land, and spoke Portuguese. They campaigned for decades to be recognised as an Indigenous people, against the opposition of local landowners, and won official recognition in 2001. Their neighbours in the region included the Maxakalí to the northeast.
